oaf: A person, especially a large male, who is clumsy or a simpleton.
oafish: Characteristic of or resembling an oaf; clumsy, stupid.
oafishness: The state or condition of being oafish; stupidity; dullness; folly.
oak: A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North America, included in genus Quercus.
oaken: Made from the wood of the oak tree.
oaklike: Resembling or characteristic of an oak or its wood.
oakmoss: Evernia prunastri, a lichen found primarily on oak trees and used in perfume.
oakum: Coarse fibres separated by hackling from flax or hemp when preparing the latter for spinning.

oarfish: A large, greatly elongated, type of fish of the family Regalecidae.
oaring: present participle and gerund of oar
oarlike: Resembling or characteristic of an oar.
oarlock: A usually U-shaped device attached to the gunwale of a rowboat to hold the oars in place while rowing.
oarsman: A person who rows a boat, either alone or with others.
oarsmanship: The skill of rowing a boat.
oasis: A spring of fresh water, surrounded by a fertile region of vegetation, in a desert.
oast: A kiln for drying tobacco, malt and especially hops.
oat: Widely cultivated cereal grass, typically Avena sativa.
oatcake: Any of many flat biscuits, or cakes, made from oatmeal.
oaten: Of, pertaining to, or made of oats.
oater: A movie or television show about cowboy or frontier life; a western movie.

oatmeal: Meal made from rolled or round oats.
